question: Raiders of the Lost Ark was the biggest hit of 1981. How many studios had turned it down?
options: None: it was an easy sell
answer: Every studio but Paramount, though it came from George Lucas and Steven Spielberg, the makers of Star Wars and Jaws. Goldman uses it to show that in Hollywood even a sure thing doesn't look sure in advance; the success that seems obvious afterwards was anything but at the time.
move: Hits look obvious only afterwards; beforehand, everyone is guessing.
trap: 'An easy sell': the famous names make it look like a sure thing.
simply: Every studio but one said no to the film that became the year's biggest hit. Afterwards, everyone said it was obviously a winner.
why: Hindsight makes success look inevitable. Remembering the rejections helps when your own idea is turned down, and when you judge other people's.
